newsitem.title: CHINA: China to use forex reserves as seller's credit.
newsitem.headline: China to use forex reserves as seller's credit.

text.p: China will use some of its rapidly growing foreign reserves as seller's credit for power projects to buy domestic power-generating systems, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
The first trial use of the credit will be for four major power projects with total capacity of 3,200 megwatts, it said, but did not identify the projects.

The credit, created by setting aside part of China's $105 billion in foreign reserves, would be used to buy power generating systems produced by plants in northeastern Harbin, Shanghai and central Sichuan province, it said.

If the system proves successful it will be expanded to other power projects, Wang Jianye, director general of the production department of the Ministry of Machine-Building, was quoted by the newspaper as saying.

Due to domestic shortages of foreign exchange and the inability of China's machinery plants to raise funds to provide credit to customers, China's power projects have turned to financially stronger foreign suppliers of power-generating machinery, the newspaper said.
The seller's credit system would help domestic manufacturers, whose share of the Chinese market for power machinery has shrunk in recent years, it said.
Last year, domestic power machinery accounted for only half the market, down from about 80 percent in the 1970s, it said.
In 1996, capacity for building about 5,000 megawatts of power generating systems lay idle, and this year the idle capacity was expected to rise to 6,000 megawatts, ministry officials warned.
